DPES-912 herdr-eventwait parity fixtures: provenance

Each directory here is one recorded case of bin/backends/herdr-eventwait.py, the Python reference
reader that `mcao herdr eventwait` must match. tests/herdr-eventwait.rs reads every case and
checks the Rust output against the recorded stdout, exit status, and subscribe request. No
expected value in that file is generated from Rust.

Reference
  file:      bin/backends/herdr-eventwait.py
  commit:    976c13e, the pin this slice checks against
  sha256:    de4dcc2e61e63694959e0848ee96920434a0becb9fa7d224d86f21836513e231
  pin note:  976c13e is taken from the sibling fixtures' provenance (util-realpath,
             util-awaiting). The DPES-864 item names no eventwait commit, so this pin is an
             inference. The same file has the same sha256 at fd4f7d4, the base of this change,
             so the recorded outputs hold for both.

Recording
  interpreter: Python 3.14.6, run as `python3 -I` (isolated mode, so no environment or
               current-directory imports).
  host:        macOS (darwin).
  generator:   a developer-only script kept outside the repository. It refuses to run unless the
               reference sha256 matches. For each case it starts a scripted fake control socket
               in a short temporary directory, runs the reference with the case's arguments, and
               writes the files below. Two independent runs produced byte-identical files.
  stderr:      the reference's stderr was kept out of the repository. It is not part of the
               contract, because the Rust messages differ.

Case files
  case.json  the scripted input, written by hand from the wire format in the reference header
             (herdr 0.7.3, protocol 16). It holds the arguments after the script name ("{socket}"
             stands for the socket path), the replies in order (a string is sent raw, any other
             value as compact JSON), and the end mode: hold keeps the connection open until the
             reference closes it, close ends after the replies, absent runs no server.
  stdout     the reference's stdout bytes.
  exit       the reference's exit status.
  request    the one subscribe line the reference sent. Absent when it never connected.

The replies were scripted, not captured from a live herdr session.

Compared as
  stdout and exit: exact. request: parsed JSON, because the reference spaces its JSON differently
  from the compact form the client sends.

Not covered (known divergences; no fixture asserts them)
  - A non-empty JSON array or object in a status field. The reference prints Python's repr, for
    example ['x'], while the Rust projection prints compact JSON. See wire.rs, field().
  - A timeout with an underscore digit separator, such as 1_0. Python's float() accepts it and
    returns 10.0, while parse_timeout rejects it.
  - The connect bound (5 seconds). It is not reproduced here: on this host (macOS) a full listen
    backlog refuses a connect rather than blocking it, so the fake server cannot trigger the
    reference's connect timeout. The Rust bound is tested in src/herdr/eventwait.rs with an
    injected connect.
